title: Getting notified about files and folders
intro: Depot tells you when the files and folders you care about change. You choose what it tells you about.

sections.heading: Follow a file
text: Every file has its own bell. Point to a file's row to show it.
steps: Click the bell icon, **Follow this file for updates**. The bell loses its slash and turns blue.
sections.tip: Depot now tells you when someone edits the file, or downloads it from a link.

sections.heading: See everything in the bell
text: Click the bell in the top bar to open **Notifications**. The newest notices are at the top.
steps: Click a notice to jump straight to the file or folder.
Click **Mark all read** to clear every unread dot.
bullets: Notices tell you when someone opens or downloads something you shared, or sends files back to you.
They also tell you when you are given access to something, or a file you follow is edited.

sections.heading: Hear about new files in a folder
text: Folders you own already tell you when a new file lands in them. You do not need to turn this on.
steps: Point to one of your folders. Its bell icon is already blue, with no slash through it.
Click the three dots at the end of the folder's row.
Click **Turn off new-file notifications** to stop. Anyone the folder is shared with can do the same for themselves.

sections.heading: Choose what the bell does
text: Click the gear in the top bar, then click **Notifications**.
steps: Turn off **Show notifications in the bell menu** to stop notices in the bell.
Turn off **Tell me when someone comes online** to stop those messages.

sections.heading: Get notices by email
text: Depot can also email you, so you hear about things even when Depot is not open. The email has a link straight to the file or folder.
To see which notices you get by email, click the gear in the top bar, then **Notifications**. Look under **Email notifications**.
steps: This list shows every notice Depot emails to you, and the address it uses.
bullets: Someone shares a file, folder or library with you.
Someone opens something you shared, the first time each person does.
Files arrive in a library or folder you follow, or through a link you sent.
A file you follow is edited.
sections.note: Your administrator chooses which emails everyone at your company gets. If the page says email isn't set up yet, ask your administrator to turn it on.
